newsitem.title: UK: UK's Littlewoods seeks to end foray abroad.
newsitem.headline: UK's Littlewoods seeks to end foray abroad.

text.p: British retail-to-football pools group Littlewoods said on Thursday it planned to sell its retail operations in Russia and India in a move to focus on core home shopping and leisure businesses.

Littlewoods, which last week resumed talks to buy Sears Plc's Freemans home shopping business, said the planned withdrawal signalled the end of its experimental foray abroad despite what it called encouraging sales in Russia and India.

"The stores halved their losses in the last 12 months but the next step would have been a step-change in the investment required to build the stores to the next level. The sensible thing is to direct resources to home shopping," a Littlewoods spokesman said.
Littlewoods, Britain's largest private company, said it had been running trial operations in western Russia since 1991 and in India since early 1996.

The British retailer has four stores in St. Petersburg, one of which has a prime position in the city's main Gostini Dvor shopping centre, and franchise operations in several other Russian cities. In all, Littlewoods employs 320 people in Russia and 120 at its store in Bangalore, India.

The spokesman said Littlewoods had talked to "one or two" interested parties about the stores but declined to give further details. He described Littlewoods' investment in its foreign retail operations as small scale.

Sales at Littlewoods International, which incorporates the group's sourcing operations and overseas retail store trials, accounted for 11 million pounds ($18.1 million) of group turnover of 2.28 billion last year.
Asked how talks with Sears were progressing, the spokesman said discussions were in a quiet phase.
"It's just a question of going through due diligence and looking at the numbers. It's still early days," he said.
Littlewoods returned to the negotiating table last week after N Brown Group Plc BWNG.L pulled out of talks with Sears.

Littlewoods had agreed in January to buy Freemans. But the deal was referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission on competition grounds and Littlewoods withdrew when it emerged Sears had talked to other potential buyers.
The Sears deal would enable Littlewoods, currently number two in the British home shopping market, to narrow the gap on Great Universal Stores Plc GUS.L.
